input: s and t are ASCII-only strings (U+0000 through U+007F), so Python code-point and JavaScript UTF-16 indexing agree. len(s) <= 4294967295 and len(t) <= 4294967294, including empty strings. For every prefix of s and every prefix of t, the number of subsequences of that source prefix equal to that target prefix must be <= 9007199254740991. Integers are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Containers are dense ordinary Arrays, excluding holes, proxies, subclasses and accessor-backed elements; strings are primitive, not boxed. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The exact number of index-distinct subsequences of s equal to t. Repeated equal characters at different positions contribute distinct choices. An empty t returns 1, including when s is empty; empty s with nonempty t returns 0.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only a private length-len(t)+1 count array is updated. Strings are immutable and no matching index sets are materialized.
numeric: The input precondition bounds every DP cell after every source prefix, not just the final answer. A zero final result can conceal enormous earlier-prefix counts and does not waive that precondition. All count additions are nonnegative and within the safe bound; lengths/indices fit Array limits. Descending target-index updates ensure each added counts[index] still belongs to the previous source prefix.
complexity: O((len(s) + 1)*(len(t) + 1)) time and O(len(t) + 1) auxiliary space, including initialization and the source scan when t is empty. Rolling counts are updated from right to left; ascending updates would incorrectly reuse one source position. No exponential subsequence enumeration is performed.
